intent: Build the smallest production-authored half of Governed Patch Reflex without creating a second NATS consumer or pretending unavailable verification capabilities are positive. Extend the closed governed request with bounded semantic intent; bind that intent to the exact delivered A2A request and current Mission Control task snapshot; call one explicit Ollama Cloud glm-5.2 lane with no provider fallback; accept only one closed full-response SEARCH/REPLACE edit for the authorized file; and persist a content-addressed provider-authorship or provider-refusal receipt before an immutable CandidateBundle. A WAL/FULL responder ledger consumes the existing bridge-owned semantic_jobs row, owns one packet lease, checkpoints exact request/provider/candidate digests, and survives restart without another model call. It starts no Mission Control attempt until a candidate is durably committed, so pre-candidate failure remains a typed non-authorizing responder refusal rather than an unfinishable governed attempt. The immutable release entrypoint and runner admit one governed-patch-responder once|serve command. The effect path remains fail-closed at Vibe/Foundry until independently pinned positive tool contracts exist.

honest_blockers: Vibe Halt has no candidate-bound dharma_swarm or generic foreign-target operation on this host; existing calibration and cooperative-child receipts cannot authorize a governed patch.
Foundry positive execution lacks both a running Docker daemon and a supervisor-pinned production image/tool provenance contract; current release child is refusal-only.
This packet stops after durable provider-authored CandidateBundle/proposal preparation and must not claim a repository effect or Mission Control terminal completion.
Governed pre-candidate failure has no parent terminal-failure contract; this packet avoids minting an attempt before candidate durability and leaves the task pending with a typed refusal.
A restart after candidate authorship may observe and continue from the old executor boot identity but must never claim the new process authored that candidate.
Every stacked PR requires external human approval before merge.
interface_mismatches: The bridge owns NATS ACK and semantic_jobs transport custody; the responder reads that durable row and must not subscribe or ACK again.
The v1 governed request binds lineage and file but not semantic intent; a new request version is required rather than silently changing v1 meaning.
A CandidateBundle proves replayable bytes and lineage, not which provider authored the edit; provider authorship requires its own closed receipt.
Provider configuration availability is not live reachability, and a served-model response is not accepted merely because the requested model was cloud-tagged.
Transport ACK, model response, candidate durability, verifier evidence, repository effect, and Mission Control completion remain distinct evidence types.
session_entry.rollback: Revert the packet-scoped responder commit. Existing bridge delivery rows, Mission Control attempts, proposals, effect fences, and terminal receipts remain untouched because this packet adds only a fail-closed candidate-authoring consumer and immutable external evidence.
